about: The v86-aarch64-v1.1 CPU profile (docs/arm64-virt-android16-plan.md, 'CPU profile' and P0.3): every ID register, the IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED choices and the differences allowed against the QEMU cortex-a35 reference. tools/cpu_contract.mjs takes the a64 profiles' expected values from this file and compares the reference's registers with it; fields are [name, high bit, low bit, value].
arm_arm: Arm Architecture Reference Manual for A-profile architecture, DDI 0487 issue L.b (the latest issue found on 2026-10-15)

hwcap.names: fp asimd evtstrm aes pmull sha1 sha2 crc32 cpuid

v2.about: v1.1 and FEAT_PAN (optional in Armv8.0; docs/arm64-virt-android16-plan.md, profile v2 and appendix F3): PSTATE.PAN, MSR PAN (immediate and register), SPSR_EL1.PAN, SCTLR_EL1.SPAN; no PAN2 (AT S1E1RP/WP) or PAN3 (EPAN). HWCAP is v1.1's (PAN has none). tests/a64/pan.mjs checks it against QEMU's -cpu max

v3.about: v2 and AArch32 at EL0 (docs/aarch32-plan.md part 1): A32, T32 with IT blocks, VFPv4 and Advanced SIMD with the crypto instructions, CP15's EL0 registers. The AArch32 ID registers are the reference's (cortex-a35) for an AArch32 at EL0 only, as Cortex-A76 reports them: no AArch32 EL1 modes (ID_PFR1.ProgMod 0), no SETEND (ID_ISAR1.Endian 0: no mixed endianness), no SMC (ID_ISAR4.SMC 0: no EL3). tests/a64/aarch32_oracle.mjs and aarch32_el0.mjs check the instructions against the reference. id_space: v1.1's registers that differ (v2's PAN included)

reference_differences.why: AArch32 at EL0 only (the reference has it at EL1 too); no SETEND, no SMC; CSV2 and CSV3 as v1.1's. The rest of the AArch32 registers is the reference's

compat_hwcap.names: half thumb fastmult vfp edsp neon vfpv3 tls vfpv4 idiva idivt lpae evtstrm
compat_hwcap.why: Linux's compat_elf_hwcap from these registers (docs/aarch32-plan.md Q0.4, checked in Q5.1 with a 32-bit /proc/cpuinfo)

id_space_rules: op0=3, op1=0, CRn=0, CRm=0: MIDR_EL1 (op2=0), MPIDR_EL1 (op2=5), REVIDR_EL1 (op2=6); every other op2 is UNDEF at every EL (as QEMU)

op0=3, op1=0, CRn=0, CRm=1-7: the registers listed; every unallocated encoding reads 0 at EL1 and is UNDEF at EL0 (Linux emulates EL0 reads with HWCAP_CPUID); Linux 6.18 reads ID_AA64MMFR3_EL1, MMFR4, ISAR3 and PFR2 unconditionally
EL0 access to the ID registers is UNDEF (EC 0x00); there is no FEAT_IDST

implementation_defined: A store crossing a page checks both pages first: a fault in either writes nothing, FAR is the first faulting byte

A load or store to a physical address with nothing mapped is a synchronous external abort (DFSC 0x10, FAR valid), as the reference (P0.2 platform probe); an address beyond the 40-bit PA range with the MMU off is an address size fault at level 0 (DFSC 0x00)
Exclusives: a 64-byte reservation granule; STXR to an address other than the LDXR's fails; exception entry does not clear the local monitor (as QEMU); ERET and CLREX clear it
TCR_EL1.TG0/TG1 naming a granule the profile does not declare, or a reserved encoding, act as 4 KiB (as QEMU's sanitize_gran_size)

HVC is taken by the emulator as PSCI 1.1 and SMCCC whatever its immediate (the reference handles HVC #1 the same); unknown function IDs return NOT_SUPPORTED (-1); SMCCC_VERSION is NOT_SUPPORTED, as the reference; SMC is UNDEF (EC 0x00)
One system counter, monotonic across cores and continuous over snapshot restore; without EL2, CNTVOFF is 0
Unallocated and out-of-profile non-hint encodings are UNDEF (EC 0x00); unimplemented HINT #0-#127 are NOPs; every DMB and DSB CRm value is a full barrier

cpu.why: v86 does not claim to be a Cortex part (reference 0x411fd040)
no AArch32: the reference runs AArch32 EL0 (probe aarch32=ran there, enoexec on v86) and /proc/cpuinfo lists 32-bit features
2 breakpoints and 2 watchpoints (reference 6, 4 and 2 context breakpoints)
the reference reads 0 and Linux reaches the same mitigations through its MIDR safe list; the vulnerabilities/* texts may differ
no mixed endianness (no big-endian data at EL1) and no Secure memory without EL3 (reference 1 and 1)

cpu.behaviour: SIMD stores (STP of Q registers, ST1-ST4) faulting across a page
cpu.why: the reference writes element by element and leaves a partial write; v86 writes nothing; tests/a64/system_oracle.mjs compares PC, ESR, FAR and registers only

cpu.behaviour: the probe's excl_aba on 2 and 4 cores
cpu.why: QEMU's STXR compares values, so an ABA write between LDXR and STXR goes unnoticed (excl_aba=0); v86 fails it (excl_aba=1)
follow from the register differences above

dtb.why: v86 writes one (the reference runs with dtb-randomness=off)
v86 has no pflash, fw-cfg, GPIO controller, power button or dynamic sysbus devices
with extended RAM v86 has two memory ranges, from 0x4000_0000 and from 4 GiB; the reference has one from 0x4000_0000 (the probe's pagemap high-page check is judged on v86 only)

behavior.instruction: DC ZVA on Device memory (the MMU off, or a Device mapping)
behavior.why: v86 takes the alignment fault the Arm ARM requires for Device memory (DDI 0487 L.b, DC ZVA); QEMU 9.2 zeroes the block (target/arm/tcg/helper-a64.c, HELPER(dc_zva))

behavior.instruction: an unaligned load or store to a Device mapping with the MMU on
behavior.why: v86 takes the Alignment fault the Arm ARM requires for any unaligned access to Device memory; the reference QEMU 9.2 (TCG on the owner's arm64 Mac) completes it (tests/a64/mmu.mjs keeps its misaligned probes on Normal memory)
AArch64.TakeException leaves NZCV as it was, as v86 does; QEMU 9.2 clears it (pstate_write in arm_cpu_do_interrupt_aarch64); tests/a64/lockstep.mjs adopts QEMU's flags at an exception entry

behavior.instruction: reads of RAM below the kernel (0x4000_0000)
behavior.why: QEMU's boot stub lives at the start of RAM; v86 starts the kernel directly and leaves it zero

behavior.instruction: debug exceptions while OSLSR_EL1.OSLK is set (it is at reset)
behavior.why: the Arm ARM disables breakpoint, watchpoint and step exceptions under the OS Lock, as v86 does; QEMU 9.2 tests OSLSR bit 0 instead of OSLK (bit 1) and never blocks them (target/arm/debug_helper.c, arm_generate_debug_exceptions)
v86 implements them on its context-aware breakpoint; QEMU 9.2 does not (LOG_UNIMP)
v86 takes the SP alignment fault (EC 0x26) the Arm ARM requires; QEMU 9.2 does not check SP alignment (an EL0 load through a misaligned SP becomes an ordinary alignment fault with the MMU off)
v86 traps it (EC 0x01) when it would wait, as the Arm ARM says; QEMU 9.2 never traps WFE (it yields)

behavior.instruction: the syndrome of a trapped MSR DAIFSet/DAIFClr at EL0
behavior.why: v86 reports the instruction's op1 3 and op2 6/7; QEMU 9.2 swaps op1 and op2 (syn_aa64_sysregtrap's arguments)
